title: Obex's Liquidity Layer can mint 100 million USDS while its burn limit, offboarding process and allocation strategy remain unspecified
content:
Two rate limits in this chunk are set: `LIMIT_USDS_MINT` at maxAmount 100,000,000 USDS with slope 50,000,000 per day (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.1.1.3.1.1.1), and `LIMIT_USDS_TO_USDC` at the same figures (…3.1.1.3). Every other listed limit defers: USDS burn (…3.1.1.2), sUSDS deposit and withdrawal (…3.1.2.1 and …3.1.2.2), `LIMIT_USDC_TO_DOMAIN` (…3.1.3.1) and `LIMIT_USDC_TO_CCTP_ETH` (…3.1.3.1.1). So do the off-chain parameters `MAINNET_MIN_OPERATION_SIZE` and `DEBT_CEILING_BUFFER` (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.1.1.2.1).

The pattern of what is set is coherent rather than random: the two configured limits are exactly the pair needed to mint USDS and convert it to USDC — the minimum viable path for putting capital to work. The unset limits govern winding down, yield-vault positions, and cross-chain movement.

That ordering is worth flagging. The burn limit in particular is the parameter used by the emergency runbook's final step. An unset limit is not necessarily a blocked one — `setUnlimitedRateLimitData` exists, and unlimited would be the sensible setting for repayment — but the Artifact does not say which state applies, so the document does not let a reader confirm that the emergency path is open.

The same deferral extends to process. "Instance Lifecycle Management" covering onboarding and offboarding "will be specified in a future iteration" (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.2.1.4), as will "Upgrading Controller" (…1.5), and the Allocation Strategy section contains only a promise of future logic (A.6.1.1.5.2.6.1.2.3). Obex can borrow and deploy 100 million USDS under documented rules; how it would retire a venue, upgrade its controller, or decide between venues is not yet written down.
description: Only the USDS mint and USDS-to-USDC swap limits carry values; burn, sUSDS deposit and withdrawal, USDC-to-domain and CCTP limits all defer to "a future iteration of the Obex Artifact".
